correctness.rationale: The explicit disjoint partition of cube plus diagonal segment into a central cube and d swept positive coordinate facets has unit Jacobians and exact mass ratios. Integrating uniform coordinates in those pieces gives zero mean and the diagonal/off-diagonal covariance entries, hence the two eigenvalues. The known volume identity and exact determinant imply the isotropic formula; logarithmic expansion is valid for fixed positive cant. Coupling fails with probability at most (delta+k a)/(delta+d a), and the standard independent-uniform CLT yields the empirical-mean limit. Exact rational and rejection checks replayed successfully on verify.py; no finite computation is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The isotropic constant and covariance operator are natural geometric invariants not specified by the known volume alone. An exact body-uniform law on the isocanted zonotope reveals a nontrivial exchangeable common-shift limit and persistent correlations as dimension grows. The universal negative logarithmic correction in the isotropic-scale expansion quantifies the quantitative approach to the cube isotropic scale despite a linearly growing diagonal covariance eigenvalue. Exact all-dimensional tensor and quantitative TV coupling are intrinsically informative, not arbitrary finite examples.
